plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with narrow silvery-green leaves and dense spikes of small tubular flowers. Widely cultivated in gardens and commercial fields for its essential oil, and loved by bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; widely cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the United States
plants.funFact: The name lavender comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans used it to scent their baths.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, coarse stem and a big flower head made of hundreds of tiny florets surrounded by yellow ray petals. Cultivated for seeds, oil, and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated in Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, France, and the United States
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds track the sun across the sky (heliotropism), but mature flower heads stop moving and generally face east.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves held above the water and spectacular flowers on tall stalks. The leaves have a self-cleaning, water-repellent surface.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (June to September) in temperate Asia
plants.location: Native to Asia and Australia; found in ponds and lakes in India, China, Japan, Vietnam, and cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds have been known to germinate after more than 1,000 years of dormancy.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody evergreen shrub that produces the largest flower head in the Protea genus, with a bowl-shaped cluster of colorful bracts surrounding a center of tiny flowers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering often occurring in midwinter (May to September) in some areas
plants.location: Native to the fynbos of the southwestern and southern Cape in South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and the genus is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change shape.
